speech.transcript: Cryptography is the art of hiding meaning. It turns a readable message into something unreadable and back again. plain text is the original intelligible message or data. Here is what you want to protect. CypherText is the transformed, unintelligible form, an attacker who sees it learns nothing useful. Encryption turns plaintext into ciphertext. Decryption turns ciphertext back into plaintext. The same process in reverse. A cipher is the algorithm for the transformation. A cryptosystem adds key management and key distribution. The algorithm alone is not enough. A key controls the transformation. It is the input to the algorithm. Key space is the set of all possible keys. A larger key space means a stronger lock. A simple example, replace each letter with the 1-3 places later. Meat becomes pHHW. That is a substitution cipher with key 3. Plan text, cipher text, cipher key, key space. These five words are the foundation of every algorithm that follows.
